messages:
alex.s: FYI customer reported sudden p99 spikes around 10:03 UTC for the /v1/generate endpoint. They attached screenshots showing p95 stable but p99 jumping to ~3s. filing support case now.

maria.t: thanks. does the dashboard alerting on p99 fire? which data source?

alex.s: alert did NOT fire. dashboard panel is using aggregated histogram rollup (prometheus histogram_quantile over rollup buckets). alert rule uses a raw export p99 from the time-series consumer. looks like mismatch.

jordan: can you paste the exact prometheus expressions and grafana panel config?

alex.s: panel query: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))  // route=/v1/generate

alert query (from alerts): 1000 * (quantile_over_time(0.99, latency_ms{route="/v1/generate"}[5m]))  // metric is latency_ms gauge from agent

priya: aha so panel is using histogram buckets in seconds and then we multiply? unit conversions maybe. also alert uses quantile_over_time on a summary-ish gauge. different aggregations.

maria.t: we need to confirm where the 3s number originates. customer screenshot is in ms though their UI shows '3s' which could be 3000ms or 3.0 on a differently scaled metric.

jordan: quick check — ingest pipeline stores buckets at aggregation_time=1m. Rollups can lose tail percentiles if buckets are coarse. If our histogram buckets end at 2s, p99 can appear as 2s or get rounded to upper bucket. do we have bucket cutoffs?

alex.s: grabbing bucket metadata from metric registry... pasted below:

- le: 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, +Inf

priya: so top explicit bucket is 2s. that explains an apparent jump to ~3s on some calculations: histogram_quantile will interpolate but if many samples fall in +Inf bucket instrumentation matters. but the alert uses a gauge so it can capture >2s values explicitly.

maria.t: then how did dashboard show ~3s at 10:03? maybe unit mismatch in panel (seconds vs ms) or a different datasource.

jordan: I checked grafana panel: unit set to seconds. but the underlying metric for the panel sometimes is the aggregated 'http_request_duration_seconds_bucket' and sometimes an exported derived 'request_latency_seconds' depending on the template variable. looks like templated variable switched to a legacy series at that time.

alex.s: confirmed in panel history — variable route_selector picked legacy metrics between 10:00-10:05 due to a recent config change in the dashboard folder. Old series reports percentiles computed client-side in ms and stored as gauge with name request_latency_ms_p99. panel displayed as seconds so it rendered 3000 as 3s. hence the visual spike.

priya: so we have two separate problems: 1) inconsistent metric families (histogram vs gauge p99) and 2) dashboard config mismatch (units). both lead to confusion and missed alerts.

maria.t: customer-facing action: explain discrepancy and reassure actual p99 from alerting path remained below SLA? which we need to verify.

jordan: I replayed the alert query against raw warehouse for 09:50-10:20. quantile_over_time shows ~420ms at 10:03, so alert path was fine.

alex.s: wrote this to support case: "Panel shows 3s due to legacy p99 gauge rendered in seconds; our alert path, which uses quantile_over_time on latency_ms, shows 420ms at spike time. We will fix dashboard and harmonize metrics." sent.

maria.t: ops actions:
- change grafana panel to explicitly use http_request_duration_seconds_bucket histogram and set unit properly (seconds) OR convert gauge from ms to seconds consistently
- add dashboard test that compares panel value to alert expression for divergence > 2x -> create alert to detect dashboard mismatch
- update instrumentation docs to discourage storing precomputed p99 gauges unless labeled as derived

priya: also adding a one-off migration plan: export legacy p99 gauges to a diagnostics table and then retire the old series. will coordinate with metrics-ingest.

jordan: short-term mitigation: I patched the panel variable to prefer histogram series and forced a refresh. pushed change to grafana repo (PR #452).

alex.s: customer updated support thread: thanks for fast reply. they want confirmation we will make alerting reflect the displayed panel or vice versa. I suggested we will make dashboard match alerting and follow up with a short statement.

maria.t: follow-ups for next week:
- priya to lead doc PR for instrumentation best-practices (templates for histogram buckets and quantile export)
- jordan to run a scan across dashboards for panels that reference request_latency_ms_p99 and list them for conversion
- alex to send customer-facing note after internal changes are merged

priya: creating todos in eng-sre board. also adding an onboarding checklist item for new services: ensure histogram has high-enough top bucket (>= 10s) or use summary gauge with explicit unit.

observability-bot: deploy bot: grafana repo PR #452 merged by jordan — change applied to production dashboards at 11:07 UTC :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: incident-metrics-checker noticed no alert gaps during 09:50-10:20 window. :thumbsup:

maria.t: closing thread once docs PR and dashboard conversions are listed. thanks everyone. :heart:

alex.s: adding final note for audit: root cause = inconsistent metric families + dashboard unit mismatch. customer impact = visual confusion only; alerting path intact. remediation steps listed above.
